:::{#thm-kernel-same-mode}
#### A density and its kernel have the same modes

If $g$ is a [kernel of a density](#def-kernel) $f$ with domain $A$,
then the modes of $f$ are exactly the elements of the [argmax](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra.html#def-argmax) of $g$:

$$x^* \text{ is a [mode](#def-mode) of } f \iff x^* \in \argmax_{x \in A} g(x).$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

Write $f(x) = c\, g(x)$ with $c > 0$ (@def-kernel).
For any $x$, multiplying both sides of $g(x^*) \ge g(x)$ by $c > 0$
gives $f(x^*) \ge f(x)$,
and dividing by $c$ reverses this.
So $f(x^*) \ge f(x)$ for every $x$ exactly when $g(x^*) \ge g(x)$ for every $x$.
By the definition of the argmax, these are the conditions $x^* \in \argmax_{x \in A} f(x)$ and $x^* \in \argmax_{x \in A} g(x)$.

:::

:::
